newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Germany's Kohl arrives for two-day Irish visit.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl arrives for two-day Irish visit.

text.p: Helmut Kohl arrived in Ireland on Wednesday for the first official bilateral visit there by a German chancellor since 1979.

The visit, part of Kohl's drive to visit smaller European Union states during the current EU review of its treaties, was also expected to underline the existing good relations between Dublin and Bonn.

Kohl was due to hold talks on Wednesday with Irish Prime Minister John Bruton. With Ireland the current EU president, the two men's discussions were expected to focus mainly on such EU issues as institutional reform, expansion of the Union and the introduction of a single currency in 1999.
Trade should figure high among bilateral topics for discussion. Germany is Ireland's second biggest European trading partner.
Later on Wednesday, Kohl -- who was accompanied to Dublin by his wife Hannelore -- was due to address the Irish parliament.

On Thursday, he is to pay a courtesy call on Irish President Mary Robinson. She was returning home later on Wednesday from an official visit to Germany, where she opened the Frankfurt Book Fair which this year has taken Ireland as its theme.
Thursday is the anniversary of Germany's 1990 reunification and Kohl was to host a Unity Day reception in the Irish capital before leaving for home.

The German Chancellor last visited Ireland in 1990 to attend a European Council meeting in Dublin Castle. He returns to Dublin on Saturday for a one-day special summit of European Union heads of government.
